paper_reason: Rudelson & Vershynin's stable-rank construction (Prop. 3.9): an m-by-n matrix formed of m/n repeats of the identity has ||W||_F = sqrt(m), sigma_max = sqrt(m/n) and stable rank exactly n. At m=64, n=16 BLME returns 8.000000000000 / 2.000000000000 / 16.000000000000 against the exact 8 / 2 / 16 (relative error 0 on all three). This is a theoretical anchor; the paper publishes no transformer measurement to reproduce.
confounds_reason: Measured over 5 models: mean_frobenius_norm rho +0.894 with d_model and +0.600 with parameter count; _meta_mean_stable_rank rho +0.894 / +0.700; norm_uniformity rho +0.894 / +0.600. These are architectural quantities by definition. mean_stable_rank_normalized does not remove the dependence, it changes its sign and strengthens it against parameter count: rho -0.671 with d_model and -0.800 with parameter count (0.0559 / 0.0595 / 0.0722 / 0.0500 / 0.0529). Independently, zero-padding diag(8,...,1) from 8x8 to 256x256 leaves Frobenius, spectral and RAW stable rank unchanged while dividing the normalized companion by exactly 32. n=5 with three distinct widths supports a direction, not a coefficient.
defects: OBSERVABILITY, weight_norms.py:109-121,165-170: failures are recorded as NaN and then removed by np.nanmean with no counter and no warning, so a layer whose SVD failed is indistinguishable from one that was never present. Adding one all-NaN 4x4 matrix beside I4 leaves all six scalar headlines bit-identical with zero diagnostics.

COMPARABILITY, weight_norms.py:148-170: the per-layer average is over EXPOSED matrices, so a fused QKV projection contributes one matrix where a split Q/K/V contributes three. Architecturally equivalent layouts therefore give different means; this is a layout confound, not an arithmetic error.

COMPARABILITY, weight_norms.py:105,199-206: mean_stable_rank_normalized divides by min(m,n), which is the right bound, but the resulting number still depends on matrix SHAPE choices (zero-padding an 8x8 to 256x256 divides it by 32 with the raw stable rank unchanged), so it should not be presented as architecture-invariant.

SCOPE: only per-LAYER parameters are measured (get_layers), so the embedding and unembedding matrices -- which WeightWatcher does report and which dominate parameter count on small models -- are outside the profile. That is a defensible scope, but it is not stated in the output.
